text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Conservatives see a possibility of selling half of the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt to Bank Austria, but Finance Minister Viktor Klima says he would sell the bank to the highest bidder as he is not prepared to miss out on three billion schillings only because of party politics.
- The 15 million schilling loss for the state due to a lack in supply of motorway passes might have to be paid back by the company supplying them.
- Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner has set an ultimatum of three weeks for Austria's energy providers to present him with draft laws for Austria's energy economy.
- Vienna airport will reduce fees for ground control for airliners Austrian Airlines, Lauda-air and Tyrolean Airways after having signed new contracts.
- The hi-jacked Austrian Airlines plane safely returned to Vienna after the hi-jacker was overpowered in Berlin.
DIE PRESSE
- Klima sees a possibility of the City of Vienna government withdrawing from Bank Austria, enabling the latter to take over Creditanstalt.
- The conservative People's Party presented opinion polls showing 57 percent of Austrians were against a takeover of Creditanstalt by Bank Austria.
- Pensions will be raised again in 1998 after having remained stable over the last two years due to the stringent austerity measures by the government.
- Austria's state debt will sink to 1,610 billion schillings in 1997, falling to 65 percent of GDP.
- After new agreements in Austria's textile industry it will be possible to work for up to 48 hours a week on a flexible basis.
KURIER
- Conservatives are planning to demand a cut of government subsidies for Bank Austria at a special session of parliament concerning the privatisation of Creditanstalt.
- Austria's austerity package reduced the country's deficit to 89.5 billion schillings in 1996, 400 million schillings below the planned deficit.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- The sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria seems certain as Klima has stated he would sell the bank to the best bidder.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- The European Commission demands complete abolition of Austria's anonymous savings accounts.
